We cannot say enough wonderful things about VCA West Los Angeles Hospital and, especially, their incredible Cardiology Team. Our Westie, Messi, recently underwent a PDA procedure, and from the very beginning, we felt that he was in the best possible hands.
The communication throughout the entire process was outstanding. Every question we had was answered promptly and thoroughly by the doctors, whether by phone or email. We received a call before the procedure, and then another call immediately afterward from the operating doctor, personally letting us know that everything had gone well. As worried dog parents, those calls meant more to us than they probably realize.
There is no question that a procedure like this is a significant financial commitment, but when it comes to the health and life of your family member, knowing that he is receiving exceptional care is priceless.
A huge and heartfelt thank-you to Dr. Liu, Dr. Garretto, Dr. Allen, and the entire Cardiology Team for taking such wonderful care of our boy. Your expertise, compassion, communication, and genuine care made an incredibly stressful experience so much easier for us.
Messi is now recovering well, and we are incredibly grateful to have our little guy home with us. He is already looking forward to the day he can run, play, and cause trouble with his two brothers again!
Thank you, VCA West Los Angeles, for taking such great care of our boy. We will always be grateful.

I also found that the prices VCA charge were much cheaper than our previous vet (center Sinai). I wish I’d gone here first. For a large vet they are very welcoming and I feel comfortable going in. They always give you a price breakdown before you’re charged and in my experience will work with you if things are unaffordable. They are my vet for life I could not recommend them anymore.

am submitting a formal complaint regarding the conduct of a staff member identified as Ralph and another front-desk employee who refused to provide her name.
My dog, Perseus, received emergency care at VCA West Los Angeles and now requires continued follow-up with Dr. Victoria Hare and the internal medicine team. I have never refused payment or indicated that I do not intend to pay for his care.
At a prior visit, I was unable to complete payment after waiting approximately 20 minutes during an emergency at the facility. I had urgent personal circumstances and faced an increasingly difficult commute to the Palisades. This was not a refusal to pay.
On Saturday, I was told by telephone that a wire transfer would be accepted for my Tuesday appointment because my trustee instructed me not to use my American Express card. I arrived 30 minutes early to obtain the wire instructions and resolve the balance before Perseus’s appointment.
Instead, I was met with resistance. Ralph spoke to me in a hostile and condescending manner and stated words to the effect of, “People like you will run up the bill and not pay.” I found this statement offensive, humiliating, and discriminatory. I believe I was treated with racial bias and would not have been spoken to this way if I were a white client.
I have been actively working to pay the balance. My funds are managed through a trustee, and a wire transfer is the appropriate, traceable payment method. A prior American Express transaction was flagged due to multiple veterinary charges made the same day during Perseus’s transfer of care; this was a fraud-prevention issue, not an attempt to avoid payment.
I request:
•	Written wire-transfer instructions so my trustee can remit payment promptly.
•	Confirmation that Perseus’s medically necessary care will continue without delay while payment is processed.
•	A prompt investigation into Ralph’s conduct and the identity of the employee who refused to provide her name.
•	Preservation of all relevant call recordings, surveillance footage, account notes, messages, and appointment records.
•	Written confirmation that neither Perseus nor I will face retaliation, delays, or barriers to care because of this complaint or payment arrangement.
Please acknowledge this complaint and provide a substantive written response within five business days

Extremely concerning experience with Dr. Rachel Garrett at VCA West Los Angeles Emergency.

I brought my 1-year-old Shiba Inu, Mochi, in because I thought she might have a tick on her neck. We are established VCA clients, and I expected the same standard of care we have received at our regular VCA hospital.

Mochi is a very friendly and social dog with no history of aggression toward people. In fact, while we were sitting in the waiting area before seeing Dr. Garrett, members of the front desk staff were interacting with and petting Mochi without any problem. People were commenting on how sweet and cute she was.

When we were finally taken into an exam room, neither Dr. Garrett nor the technician physically examined Mochi or touched the area I was concerned about. I held Mochi and lifted her neck myself to show them the spot. I was then told it was a tick and that Mochi would need to be sedated to remove it because she was “aggressive.”

I was shocked. Neither Dr. Garrett nor the technician had made a meaningful attempt to approach, touch, or interact with her. Mochi did not lunge, snap, growl at, or attempt to bite anyone.

When I questioned why she was being labeled aggressive without even being approached, Dr. Garrett told me that Mochi had looked at her as though she wanted to bite her and said she would not “risk her life” trying to remove the supposed tick without sedation.

This entire interaction occurred in front of my 9-year-old daughter, who witnessed the way our dog was being described and the conversation about sedating her.

I then became even more concerned because Mochi had not been weighed and, to my knowledge, basic vitals had not been obtained. I specifically asked Dr. Garrett whether she was saying that she did not need Mochi’s heart rate or blood pressure before sedating her. Dr. Garrett told me that she did not need those vitals to perform the proposed sedation. I asked again because I wanted to make sure I had understood her correctly, and she again confirmed this to me.

At that point, I refused sedation and left.

What makes this experience particularly concerning is that VCA’s own medical record confirms that no physical examination was performed. Dr. Garrett’s note states:

“No PE performed. Unable to touch dog.”

The same record lists Mochi’s weight as “n/a.”

I immediately took Mochi to another emergency veterinary hospital that same evening.

The experience there was completely different. Their staff calmly approached and handled Mochi, obtained her vitals, and performed a physical examination. They used a muzzle as a reasonable safety precaution, which I had absolutely no objection to.

Their veterinarian was able to examine the exact area on Mochi’s neck without sedation.

And the result was the most disturbing part of this experience:

There was no tick. It was a small scab.

No sedation was necessary. No diagnostics were necessary. No treatment was necessary.

I completely understand that veterinary professionals must protect themselves from potential bites. I have no objection whatsoever to reasonable restraint, a muzzle, or even sedation when it is actually necessary for an animal’s safety or the staff’s safety.

What I cannot understand is how sedation could be recommended to remove a presumed tick when the dog had not even been physically examined and the lesion itself had not been physically examined.

Had I simply trusted the recommendation and consented, my one-year-old dog potentially could have been sedated to remove something that was not even a tick.

I have filed a formal complaint with VCA and am submitting the documentation from both hospitals to the California Veterinary Medical Board for independent review.

This was the most concerning experience I have ever had with a veterinarian, and based on this experience, I would not allow Dr. Rachel Garrett to treat my dog again.

Our dog is worse after a week of hospitalization than when the dog was admitted. 5 figures spent so far. No answers. But here's why VCA truly fails:

-- six to eight different doctors caring for the dog. Every day it's like starting over and they LOSE important details of the case in a telephone game.

--they put a dog with active bleeding GI tract on a psyllium husk supplement without telling us.This is like rubbing gravel on an open wound. That's the day the dog took a downturn.
--they also put the dog on an FOS (fructooligosaccharides) supplement this is also an irritant in a dog with a gut infection. It actually feeds the bad bacteria present.

You don't have to take my word for it. Ask every AI out there: Grok, Gemini, ChatGPT - all of them. If they all agree that these supplements shouldn't be given to a dog with an active bloody GI infection, then that means it's common knowledge.

These are supplements only for those whose guts are in OK shape. Otherwise, they're irritants and can feed the pathogen. The fact that the multiple doctors DO NOT KNOW THIS is a travesty.

We brought our senior munchkin cat Doy to VCA West Los Angeles Animal Hospital on 3/10, and I truly don’t know where to begin.

We had accidentally booked the wrong date for our appointment, but when we arrived and they saw Doy’s condition, the front desk immediately stepped in and admitted him through emergency. That alone meant so much to us during such a stressful moment.

We came here after a difficult experience with another vet, where we were told Doy likely had abdominal cancer and were essentially pushed toward either immediate euthanasia or aggressive testing, without much space to process or consider what was best for him. We left that appointment emotionally overwhelmed and unsure.

Coming to VCA changed everything for us. We were incredibly fortunate to meet Dr. Ponkey, who was truly a godsend. The very first thing she did was ask about our understanding of Doy’s condition before offering her own perspective. She then walked us through everything with clarity, compassion, and honesty. What stood out the most was how she balanced medical expertise with genuine empathy.

She also openly shared what she would do if Doy were her own cat, which helped guide us in such an uncertain time. Most importantly, she respected our wishes. When we expressed that we didn’t want to proceed with invasive procedures if the ultrasound results were not promising, she listened and honored that without pressure.

In the end, we chose comfort care — something we had been trying to advocate for from the beginning. Dr. Ponkey supported us fully and prescribed medications to keep Doy comfortable, including an appetite stimulant, anti-nausea meds, and steroids.

Because of her care, we were able to spend two more meaningful months with Doy. He continued to enjoy the little things he loved, and we got to cherish that time as a family.

Doy passed peacefully on 4/29, at home, surrounded by all of us — no suffering, no fear. And we truly believe that outcome was only possible because of the guidance and compassion we received here.

We are forever grateful to Dr. Ponkey and the team at VCA West LA for giving us not just more time, but the right kind of time.
(Adding photos of Doy’s “borrowed days” — moments we’ll treasure forever.)

They have a Director in there who does seem to know what he’s doing, but they still assigned a brand-new grad to my dog, who is a high-risk cardiac patient, and she openly admitted she knew nothing about cardiac care to me. She couldn’t answer my questions, and when I questioned her abilities because of it, she was petty and put in my dog’s records that the “owner was untrusting of their care and kept asking questions and to see patient.”

Um yeah, that’s because ChatGPT was answering my questions while you went to the back to “find out” every time and then came back to me with the same answer AI did. Several times when she couldn’t answer a question, she’d get the Director; he’d come out and answer as if she had answered it already and I wasn’t understanding, and he was “annoyed,” like he had to repeat himself. Sir, you clearly had no clue she was telling me “I don’t know,” and she was clearly going to the back and telling him she had given me answers and that I wanted him to reassure me or something. Not the case. I found out she had just passed the vet board exam 10 months prior and clearly wasn’t ready to be on her own in a busy ER—at least not to be assigned to high-risk cardiac patients.

And don’t get me started with their Cardiology team. I brought my dog to the ER at 7 AM due to him fainting. They took five hours to check his heart. In addition, they refused to check him until I agreed to abandon his cardiologist he had for many years and transfer care to them permanently.

I am heartbroken writing this.

My dog Zip was my companion for 16 years — my little shadow, my comfort, my family. She trusted me to protect her, and I trusted VCA to help me care for her. What happened instead has been devastating.

Zip had known kidney disease, with a creatinine around 3 (Stage 3). Despite this, she was diagnosed with congestive heart failure without proper confirmation — no echocardiogram was done. Based on that unverified diagnosis, she was treated with medications, including diuretics, that can put significant strain on the kidneys.

Shortly after, she went into acute kidney failure.

Instead of stabilizing her, her condition declined rapidly. I watched her weaken, knowing something wasn’t right, but trusting the medical decisions being made.

Her first hospitalization cost about $5,500. As things worsened, I had no choice but to continue care at ASEC (also part of VCA), where I spent another $35,000–$40,000 trying desperately to keep her alive with fluids and intensive support.

Despite everything, she did not survive.

I want to be fair — Dr. Hare was kind and compassionate, and I am grateful for her humanity during previous hospitalizations .

But my experience with the cardiology department was extremely disappointing, and at times felt careless. I also experienced a lack of basic compassion from management. Despite already leaving about a $4,000 deposit and having spent tens of thousands of dollars with VCA over the years, I was not allowed to briefly go home to retrieve my credit card to pay a remaining $1,600 balance. In a moment of crisis, that felt cold and inhumane.

What haunts me most is that a simple echocardiogram could have confirmed — or ruled out — heart failure before exposing her to treatment that carried known risks for her kidneys. That step was taken after administering the medication that put Zip in acute kidney failure .

I trusted them with her life.

Zip deserved careful, thoughtful medical decisions. She deserved a chance.

Instead, I lost her — and I will always wonder if things could have been different.

She was my heart, my shadow, my world — and a piece of me left with her.

Dr. Sarah Nugen took great care of our dog when he had an infection. The wait time was also very short and the facility was professional and clean.

Dr. Liu and the team at the Cardiology department - THANK YOU, from the deepest down of our hearts.

I brought in my dog, Charlie,  after being referred to the emergency department by my local veterinarian and I am so so so grateful that they did. We admitted to VCA late at night with our dog in critical condition following multiple seizures. In short: Stay away! Go to the 24/7 ER on Wilshire in Santa Monica (I’ve never been but it gets glowing reviews) never agree to anything before getting a second opinion (even if it is on ChatGPT)! They are crooks just after your money. VCAs are a chain after one thing, and it’s not your pets best interest.

They charge $50 fee to fill a prescription. 30pills of prednisone is $5 on 1800PetMeds. It’s $55 at VCA. Do NOT get any medications from them. They know that people are usually in dire need when they are there so they charge these exorbitant fees to extract money out of you.

Expect to be there 2+ hrs no matter what the reason is for your visit. They will try and get you to run every test under the sun (to get money out of you) rather than simply treat what is most likely the problem.
I don’t want to go into too much detail, but I would look to go anywhere else but this facility. There is a 24hr emergency vet on Wilshire I will be going to moving forward should I need to.
This place is a joke.
Some staff are extremely knowledgeable, kind and considerate (Dr Sammut), but still after your money mainly….while others seem like they are still in training and completely in over their heads (Dr Kumar), and that is being extremely polite.
When I go in and spend $350+ on an “exam” only, I expect expert level care. That is not a guarantee here and that’s unacceptable.
My advice: go somewhere else. If that’s not an option, get a second opinion (even if it’s just by phone) because it’s highly likely they are just scaring you into tests that will cost thousands of dollars and are completely unnecessary.
(I asked for the director of the facility to call me after my most recent visit. 10 days later, no one has called).
Someone recently recommended Modern Animal to me, and I plan to check them out. It’s not emergency vet service, but they say the Dr.’s are after your dogs best interest and not just money.

I have been meaning to write this review for a while! My dog, Bear, has been a patient at the VCA West LA for a several years (mainly for his vaccines, routine appointments, etc) and we love it there. The front desk team and the vet techs are always super friendly and helpful.

Last fall, Bear needed his 2nd TPLO surgery and we were referred internally to Dr. Rosselli for his procedure. Dr. Rosselli is truly an angel. She made us feel at ease from the first appointment and you can tell she sincerely cares for her patients. Bear's surgery and recovery all went perfectly. In the days following surgery, Dr. Rosselli called to check in on him and throughout the healing process was communicative and responsive to questions. We recommended her to a friend whose dog needed this same procedure and we would recommend her to anyone!
Drs. Hayward, Davila and Rosselli provided amazing care to our wonderful girl - Kate.  They embody professionalism mixed with compassion.  Thank you!

This place is one of a kind. Please please take your pet there for an emergency day or night. We received the most incredible help during the most stressful night of our lives while visiting family in LA. Our dog ran away and got hit by a car on Venice Blvd. A black dog crossing Venice at 9pm while you are on vacation in a strange place. Worst Nightmare. A Good Samaritan couple happened to witness it all, care for our dog, call us from the name on her tag and call VCA West LA letting them know Lily was on the way. They had recently been there and referred us and I am forever grateful they did. We would not know where to go and would have wasted precious time. Truly a miracle they were there when it happens.
VCA was simply amazing from the moment Lily arrived. Every staff member, every doctor and staff member. OMG I wish we had a VCA like this near our home.
We got updates and answers around the clock from the doctor herself. 3am she called us to let us know the test results and care plan.
There was compassion even when the discussion had to be about finances and payment. We never felt robbed though and even got a $1500 refund at check out. Very honest!!
We got to visit with Lily twice for as long as we wanted to. That was so special for us and for her. She has never been away from us so I am sure that helped her a lot.
The facilities are amazing also. Parking garage open day and night so one less stress when you are already at your peak. Security guard walking around. Comfortable waiting room and even a patio to get some fresh air.
I cannot say enough good things. Have this place on your address book so you are ready when a crisis strikes.
Thank you VCA Weat Los Angeles. Forever grateful!!

Zero star.

I transferred my ~ 5-6 y.o. cat to West LA VCA for the treatment of DKA and kidney infection a couple weeks ago. She was dehydrated and had severe electrolyte imbalance due to DKA and kidney problem which could not be managed by her regular vet.

After paying a hefty deposit, almost $10k, they admitted her. They charged $4-6k a day. Beside the ~$900 a day hospital stay, they charged everything à la carte. They pushed for useless tests (that are not consistent or matched for a young cat with the medical conditions). While her infection was improved and electrolytes and kidney function returned to normal, she was in the diuretic phase of acute kidney injury (AKI). She produced large volume of urine due to the kidneys not able to concentrate.

I visited her daily for several days. She was always sedated and not very responsive. She did gave me some meows. I was hoping for a recovery and anticipated to take her home in a week or two.

Over the weekend, I continued to get updates on her. Sadly,  I could not make it to see her. 😪  When asked 'how is she?' , I always get a response 'static.' Basically my cat was not responding physically.

Due to large amount of money spent, my credit was frozen over the weekend. I explained to the billing staff hoping that they would understand. No. They expected the bill to be paid daily with no exception. I asked to speak to the manager. Instead, the vet called me stating that the manager is not available over the weekend. He told me that they don't accept promissory note due to my cat's grave condition. I begged him to continue to treat my cat and told him that I would continue to make the payment knowing that my cat needed a few more days of treatment.

I was able to come up with the payment. An hour later, I got a call for the same billing staff telling me that my cat's treatment was discontinued and I have up to 6 p.m. to take her out of their hospital either to transfer her to another hospital (because their hospital is the most expensive in the area) or to take her home with me. I told her that I spoke with the vet and told him that I would like to continue the treatment. Apparently, they did not see my payments so they were about to discard my cat because she was not worth anything to them even though I had spent over $25k so far.

The staff checked and apologized for the mistake. The vet continued to perform unnecessary tests, which I permitted just to entertain him.

I was asleep and the phone was not in a different room. Around 1 a.m., I received a call stating that my cat's blood pressure was low. They needed to bolus her with more IV fluids. About an hour later, I got another call stating that my cat now has breathing difficulties. She had fluids in her lungs, pericardial sac, abdomen, etc. I know that she was malnourished for not eating regular meals for over a week. Her albumin was low. That could cause some fluids to leak into interstitial spaces due to not having enough oncotic (from albumin) pressure to hold fluids inside the blood vessels. It was most likely that they gave her too much IV fluids. She was literally drowning and that was why she was having difficulty breathing.  My cat passed away.

This is for the night emergency crew. We had an emergency with our boy Gunner and they took care of everything to make him comfortable. We had to put him down and the experience with VCA made it easier to cope with because they were patient and considerate.

We had our 1 year old great dane have her laparoscopic spay and gastropexy done here. The surgical team was great, and the email follow ups were wonderful. Thank you guys fir taking care of our Roula!

Dr Traci Hayward helped us tremendously with our cat. She diagnosed him within hours. He had terminal cancer, but Dr Hayward prescribed all the medication to keep him comfortable.  She is a very compassionate and thorough doctor and we were so lucky to get her for our cat's care.

Horrible, horrible, horrible! I would rate zero stars if I could.
Stay away from this facility at all costs. I took my family dog here to get services because he was literally dying. Tell me why this facility was more worried about a balance I owed on this account instead of giving my beloved pet the care he needs. I paid the balance first before having to pursue any treatment because they made it clear that they weren't going to prioritize his needs until I paid my bill. SMFH! These people are cold and heartless, to say the least. In the end, l ended up having to euthanize my baby. I could tell the doctors and the admin staff really didn't care about the experience they provided to me.
Shame on you VCA. I'll take my money and business elsewhere. Everyone, be warned. This place doesn't care about you, and your beloved pet. What a joke for a business and a disgusting place to take your loved ones during their last moments.

I want to express my gratitude to Dr. Justin Allen and Dr. Megan Doan at VCA West Los Angeles Animal Hospital for the exceptional care they provided to our Chihuahua, Charlie. This week, they performed a heart procedure on her, and while everything seemed fine when we returned home, she experienced some distress later that night.

At 3:30 a.m., I called the hospital, and Celina was truly amazing. She asked thoughtful questions, provided sound advice, and guided us to administer a specific medication. Within 45 minutes, Charlie was much better.

With a flight home to Seattle scheduled for 12:30 p.m. the following day, I was worried about time, but Dr. Doan made room for us that morning, carefully assessing Charlie and giving her additional medication. Since then, she has been doing wonderfully.

The hospital is well-run and staffed by compassionate professionals. Dr. Allen and Dr. Doan were not only highly skilled but also excellent communicators—professional, empathetic, and genuinely invested in Charlie’s well-being. I highly recommend them and VCA West Los Angeles Animal Hospital for any pet in need of expert care.

Miranda and the whole staff helped save my cat’s life when she went missing and treated her with amazing care and respect- and made sure she’s healthy. I’m lucky there is such great staff at VCA. They truly would do anything for animals. I could not be more grateful for the clinic staff, especially Miranda on the 2nd floor who helped arrange our reunion. Thank you VCA!!!

This hospital is exceptionally expensive. Dr. Robertson was knowledgeable but I got the strong vibe that she was judging me. Exam is twice that of other vets, and treatment is significantly more costly as well. Taking my bunny somewhere else.
VCA is organized, professional, operationally fantastic. Dr. Kaplan is a dream and I won't be going anywhere else! Grateful to have found this fantastic place full of caring, thoughtful people.

I brought my sick dog there for y rays! He ate a ball! The told me that there was no obstruction! I took him home but then took him to his veterinarian hospital were to clearly saw the obstruction and were baffled that this well known hospital overlooked it! Never again it is overpriced and a very cold loveless hospital for my beloved pet

We turned to VCA West LA for our dog Murphy’s oral melanoma diagnosis and radiation therapy. We were able to get our first oncology appointment within a week of calling, and begin radiation a couple weeks later. Both Dr. Gabrielle Carter and Dr. Brittney Stanton were incredibly compassionate, knowledgeable, and attentive. Each week, they adjusted his care plan based on even small changes to make sure he was as comfortable as possible.

After completing radiation, we brought Murphy to the emergency room three times—once for vestibular symptoms, and twice more during a sudden decline. Each time, we were seen quickly as a walk-in, and the vets explained every option thoroughly, without rushing us. They did everything they could for him as an outpatient (our choice), and thanks to their support, Murphy was able to pass at home with us.

The hospital is clean, organized, and staffed by people who clearly care. It’s expensive, but we never felt pressured. After Murphy passed, we received a handwritten card signed by the entire care team. That gesture meant everything.
Dr Robertson was amazing! She was compassionate and knowledgable and took great care of guinea pig in the last hours of his life.

I was recommended to come to their oncology department after learning my dog had cancer. I’ve never experienced a dog with cancer before and I wanted to give him the best treatment possible. I was under the impression their oncologist specialist could be trusted to not cause further harm. It was never disclosed to me that taking a cytology sample or biopsy sample would dramatically increase the spread of the cancer. The cytology report was inconclusive ultimately. So we drove four hours out of town, got no definitive answers and drastically worsened my dogs condition. His tumor went from the size of a golf ball to fully encompassing his neck in two days. They wanted to cut the tumor out and do radiation with no idea of the outcome. I’m glad I didn’t spend the 30k to promote more suffering in my dog, and I greatly regret trusting this facility. I highly recommend a holistic vet over this corporate monster.

Hi there, we're truly sorry that your experience didn’t meet expectations. We understand how important your pet’s care is. Our Hospital Manager would love the opportunity to listen to and address your concerns. Please don’t hesitate to reach out at reviews.vcawestlahospital@vca.com - we’re here for you. 💙  …
Dr. Kaplan and Stephanie were so gentle, kind and thoughtful with my kitty, I really appreciated how comfortable they made him while we visited, and their expertise!

Our dog has experienced unexplained seizures vs syncope. We brought him to this ER. The doctor seemed to offer hospitalization while also repeatedly saying he doesnt meet criteria, provided vague answers regarding the onset of a loading dose of Keppra, repeatedly talking about how short staffed they are and unsure when it may happen, offered for us to take him home, give him PO keppra, then bring back if any episodes happen again (we live 30 minutes away). I gave 2 stars for timeliness because he was seen quickly and the vet came and checked in within the hour. Got slapped with a $291 bill for essentially telling us theres not much we can do, were short staffed, and we may or may not be able to see the cardiologist even if he were to stay.
I am changing my review based on the cardiologist department. They have been amazing to me and my cat. Thank you for all that you do.
Great care disregard the bad reviews this place is great
Omg, Dr. Rue is such a gem. She clearly cares and is a lovely lady with so much patience and calmness. It’s such a relief to have someone caring for your baby when they are in pain.
Our first visit! We loved the place, great service, I highly recommend it 👍 …
Wow we felt this was our only option in an emergency. I didn’t know price gouging like this was legal. Avoid going here unless absolutely necessary.

I took my cat Luna for an emergency visit since her tail had to be amputated. This hospital tries to take you for all your worth… that’s for sure. They made it seem like they could potentially save her tail and that I had to leave her overnight to be seen quickly by the surgeon. It was almost 5 thousand in total without even the surgery. They claimed they flushed and cleaned out her maggots from her injury but when I went to another hospital for the much needed amputation, they found more maggots in her wound. Just to clean her wound and for pain meds alone it was almost 700. The least they could do was clean her wound properly considering I was there for almost 9 hours. I’m glad I backed out of paying that absurd amount because they were so willing for me to go into debt and some of their front desk people were not very detailed about their explanations. I felt like I was stuck and forced to choose them for their services but I’m glad I didn’t and chose a low cost hospital. I understand the long wait time, but the least they could’ve done was clean her wound properly… at that point I should’ve just waited until the next day to take my cat to where I have her now.

But nonetheless… I don’t think I would go back. It’s expensive and they don’t try to work with you or give you options. They don’t even try to give you low cost options!!! No mention of it until I went back and canceled their high cost service to just take Luna elsewhere. I’m really disappointed by their treatment of my cat. I expected more compassion and patience with the questions I had. There were a few nice people up front but I feel like some of the workers didn’t care enough to let me know of other options, they obviously just care about the money.

Knowing my dog ​​had no hope because she had suffered a stroke, they charged me $3,000 for one night, and it hadn't even been 12 hours before they wanted to charge me more for medication for a dog that didn't even weigh 2 pounds. I don't recommend them.
The staff was knowledgeable and courteous every step of the way, especially in a very difficult time on a complex case for our French bulldog.

Had a very late night emergency with my baby Benji. With the stress of the LA fires was so much. The doctor and nurses went above and beyond. They took such good care of him and he came home with me so happy and cuddly. Thank you so much😸 …

The receptionist, Concepcion, will tell the vet behind your back that you have requested services that you did not, and they will tell you the same exact thing that the Poison Control Helpline will tell you, for an extra $290. The biggest veterinary scam in LA County. Do not recommend, and hold onto your wallet. I have never encountered a more greedy veterinary office in my entire life. They know exactly what they are doing.

We took our cat here for an ultrasound and they insisted that we left him with them for a few hours until someone would be available (which didn’t sit well with us because of how scared he would be without us) but we eventually agreed and they had him for about 3 hours.
I don’t know how they keep animals in there, but our cat came back with fleas, which infested our whole house. Huge headache to deal with, especially while having a baby.

The services were ok, but the fact that you risk your pet catching something there because of unsanitary conditions is a reason to never go back here again and NEVER recommend this place to anyone.

I wish I could leave individual reviews for the different doctors I worked with versus an overall score because I had night and day experiences based off the doctors I interacted with. To start out with the good, Dr. Doran and everyone in neurology are amazing. When nobody believed in the viability of my dogs survival she did. She listened to all my concerns, answered all of my questions with patience, compassion, and empathy. I was so lucky to be turned over to her or else my dog wouldn’t be alive. She is a true hero. I also interacted with Dr. Jasper in the ER who was a saint, equally as kind, smart and caring. Also there’s a lot of support staff who are angels that work there. The faculty is clean, state of the art, and quite impressive.
Now the bad. Originally we were assigned to Dr. Owen. From the moment I met with her I could feel her condescending attitude towards me. She is the type of person who is nice/nasty. She’ll speak to you with obligatory kindness. Meanwhile insulting you in veiled ways. I was emotional wrecked and vulnerable and she tried to get me to put my dog down the entire time I worked with her. She made me feel bad for holding out and waiting to see if he would stabilize. And talked to me like an idiot. She’s the type of person who weaponizes her position and education. Thank God I didn’t listen to her. My dog is well on the path to recovery and making leaps and bounds in his progress daily. I’m so happy I got turned over to another doctor. I hope whoever reads these reviews will relay the message to Dr. Owen that she is a “C-U-Next-Tuesday” and I picked up on her energy from jump. I just had to play nice until I got assigned a different neurologist. Good luck to all the pet parents out there who get stuck in my situation, please don’t hesitate in taking them to VCA West LA. Overall my experience and my dogs most importantly were great. With the exception of Nurse Ratchet/ aka Dr. Owen.
